paper.title: Systematic study of the half-lives of nuclear bound-state β − \beta^{-} decay
paper.abstract: Abstract Nuclear bound-state β − \beta^{-} decay ( β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay) is a novel weak-interaction process that becomes possible when atoms are highly ionized, such as in stellar environments or heavy‑ion storage rings. In this work we present a systematic theoretical calculations for the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives of interesting candidates for the first time, where both allowed Gamow-Teller transitions and first-forbidden transitions are taken into account by the microscopic projected shell model, and the lepton phase space is calculated by the Takahashi-Yokoi model. We analyzed the structure informations for hundreds of nuclei near the β \beta -stability line, and select 16 interesting candidates belonging to two categories, i.e., nuclei with negative Q Q values and positive Q Q values in neutral atoms respectively. Among these candidates, we recommend Am 95 + 243 {}^{243}\mathrm{Am}^{95+} , Os 76 + 194 {}^{194}\mathrm{Os}^{76+} , Ac 89 + 227 {}^{227}\mathrm{Ac}^{89+} , Ra 88 + 228 {}^{228}\mathrm{Ra}^{88+} , Pu 94 + 241 {}^{241}\mathrm{Pu}^{94+} , Cm 96 + 247 {}^{247}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} and Cm 96 + 250 {}^{250}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} as promising ones for future studies of storage-ring experiments because their β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives are predicted to be much shorter than the half-lives in neutral atoms. These findings provide essential nuclear inputs for astrophysical models and identify specific candidates where experimental verification would be most valuable.

sections.heading: I Introduction
sections.text: Nuclear bound-state β − \beta^{-} decay is one of the novel weak-interaction processes. Different from the continuum β − \beta^{-} decay ( β c \beta_{\text{c}} decay, as shown in Eq. ( 1 a)) where the electron and antineutrino are emitted into the continuum states, in the bound-state β − \beta^{-} decay ( β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay, see Eq. ( 1 b)) provided that atoms get highly ionized to be hydrogen-like or even bare nuclei, the electron is not emitted to the continuum but occupying directly the bound states of electron orbitals of daughter atoms [ 1 ] . X N 0 + Z A {}^{A}_{Z}\text{X}_{N}^{0+} → \displaystyle\rightarrow Y N − 1 1 + Z + 1 A + e − + ν ~ e , {}^{\ \ \ A}_{Z+1}\text{Y}_{N-1}^{1+}+e^{-}+\tilde{\nu}_{e}, (1a) X N Z + Z A {}^{A}_{Z}\text{X}_{N}^{Z+} → \displaystyle\rightarrow Y N − 1 Z + Z + 1 A + ν ~ e , {}^{\ \ \ A}_{Z+1}\text{Y}_{N-1}^{Z+}+\tilde{\nu}_{e}, (1b) The exotic β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay channel is possible in stellar environments with high temperature or in heavy-ion storage rings where heavy atoms get highly ionized. The nuclear β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay is important for understanding the nature of neutrinos and the slow ( s s -) neutron-capture processes [ 2 ] . The concept of the β b \beta_{b} decay was first proposed by Daudel et al. in 1947 [ 3 ] . A practical theoretical framework for calculating the β b \beta_{b} -decay half-life of highly ionized atoms was developed by Takahashi and Yokoi in the 1980s [ 4 ] . Over the past decades, experiments at heavy-ion storage rings were conducted and β b \beta_{\text{b}} decays have been observed sequentially in 163 Dy 66+ [ 5 ] , 187 Re 75+ [ 6 ] , 207 Tl 81+ [ 7 ] and 205 Tl 81+ [ 8 , 9 ] . More important candidates of the nuclear β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay are expected to be detected and studied, for which theoretical calculations and analysis should be meaningful. Theoretically, calculations of the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives are basically based on the Takahashi-Yokoi model [ 4 ] where nuclear transition strengths, including both allowed and forbidden transitions, are indispensable key inputs. However, in most of the relevant calculations, unknown nuclear transition strengths are not from sophisticated nuclear many-body calculations, but estimated empirically either from the inverse electron-capture (EC) data, or from the systematics of transitions of neighboring nuclei with available data (from ground states or isomers) [ 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 ] . The former is limited to transitions from ground states of EC parent nuclei, while the latter prescription has been challenged by modern charge-exchange reactions [ 14 ] or shell-model calculations [ 15 ] . This is because most of the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay candidates are heavy nuclei and it is challenging to describe the allowed and forbidden transitions of heavy nuclei. Recently, we developed the traditional projected shell model (PSM) [ 16 , 17 ] to consider extended quasiparticle (qp) configuration space [ 18 , 19 ] , and then to describe allowed Gamow-Teller (GT) transition [ 20 , 21 ] and first-forbidden transition [ 22 ] of nuclear β \beta decay, with the help of the Pfaffian and other algorithms [ 23 , 24 , 25 ] . The extended PSM method is then combined with the Takahashi-Yokoi model to provide a microscopic method to calculate the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives for the first time [ 26 ] . Accordingly, the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives of 163 Dy 66+ and 187 Re 75+ are described successfully and the half-life of 205 Tl 81+ is predicted [ 26 ] . Further systematic calculations and research should be meaningful and beneficial for future experimental studies. In this work, we apply the PSM and Takahashi-Yokoi model to provide a systematic study of the half-lives of nuclear β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay. By analyzing the Q Q values and levels for hundreds of nuclei near the β \beta -stability line on the chart of nuclides, we selected, in addition to the three examples of 163 Dy 66+ , 187 Re 75+ and 205 Tl 81+ examined in the previous study [ 26 ] , sixteen examples for further investigation. These examples are Ir 77 + 193 {}^{193}\mathrm{Ir}^{77+} , Au 79 + 194 {}^{194}\mathrm{Au}^{79+} , Tl 81 + 202 {}^{202}\mathrm{Tl}^{81+} , Po 84 + 213 {}^{213}\mathrm{Po}^{84+} , At 85 + 215 {}^{215}\mathrm{At}^{85+} , Rn 86 + 222 {}^{222}\mathrm{Rn}^{86+} , Am 95 + 243 {}^{243}\mathrm{Am}^{95+} , and Bk 97 + 246 {}^{246}\mathrm{Bk}^{97+} , as well as Os 76 + 194 {}^{194}\mathrm{Os}^{76+} , At 85 + 212 {}^{212}\mathrm{At}^{85+} , Ac 89 + 227 {}^{227}\mathrm{Ac}^{89+} , Ra 88 + 228 {}^{228}\mathrm{Ra}^{88+} , Pu 94 + 241 {}^{241}\mathrm{Pu}^{94+} , Cm 96 + 247 {}^{247}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} , Bk 97 + 249 {}^{249}\mathrm{Bk}^{97+} , and Cm 96 + 250 {}^{250}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} . Among these, Am 95 + 243 {}^{243}\mathrm{Am}^{95+} , Os 76 + 194 {}^{194}\mathrm{Os}^{76+} , Ac 89 + 227 {}^{227}\mathrm{Ac}^{89+} , Ra 88 + 228 {}^{228}\mathrm{Ra}^{88+} , Pu 94 + 241 {}^{241}\mathrm{Pu}^{94+} , Cm 96 + 247 {}^{247}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} and Cm 96 + 250 {}^{250}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} are recommended for future storage-ring experiments due to their much shorter β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives compared to the half-lives in neutral atoms. The paper is organized as follows. In Sec. II we introduce briefly the basic framework for calculating the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-life of highly ionized atoms. The systematic calculations and predictions are discussed in details in Sec. III , and we finally summarize our work in Sec. IV .

sections.heading: III Calculations and Analysis
sections.text: In this section we provide our systematic calculations of nuclear β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives of interesting candidates. As can be seen from Eq. ( 3 ) that Q β b Q_{\beta_{\text{b}}} usually differs from Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} . When atoms get highly ionized to be hydrogen-like or even bare nuclei in stellar environments or heavy-ion storage ring, the produced electron during β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay can occupy the K K -shell orbitals of the daughter atom. In such a case, as B e − K B_{e^{-}}^{K} is usually larger than Δ ​ B e − \Delta B_{e^{-}} , Q β b Q_{\beta_{\text{b}}} is then usually larger than Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} . This indicates that, on one hand, a stable atom with negative Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} would become an unstable nucleus if Q β b Q_{\beta_{\text{b}}} is positive and then the β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay channel is available in highly ionized environments. Typical examples of this type and the corresponding Q Q -value information can be seen from Table 1 . On the other hand, for some nuclei that can β c \beta_{\text{c}} decay with small Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} value, the increased Q β b Q_{\beta_{\text{b}}} would enable transitions to more low-lying states of the daughter nucleus, which may lead to totally different β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay rate compared with β c \beta_{\text{c}} -decay rate. Typical examples of this type and the corresponding Q Q -value information can be seen from Table 2 . Before systematic calculations, we analyzed the Q Q -value information and excitation levels for hundreds of nuclei near the β \beta -stability line on the nuclear chart, and selected promising candidate nuclei according to the above two categories. For the first category with negative Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} but positive Q β b Q_{\beta_{\text{b}}} , except for the two examples of 163 Dy and 205 Tl that have been studied in Ref. [ 26 ] , as well as the two special examples of 148 Eu and 244 Pu for which the corresponding transitions are fifth forbidden transitions so that the β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay should be negligible, all the remaining candidates are listed in Table 1 . The second category consists of nuclei that are already β − \beta^{-} -unstable in the neutral atoms ( Q β c > 0 Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}}>0 ), for which the β b \beta_{\text{b}} channel provides additional decay paths to low-lying states of the daughter nucleus. In this case, since for large Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} value, the β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay channel would be negligible compared with the β c \beta_{\text{c}} decay channel because the latter has a much larger lepton phase space than the former, accordingly, we restrict our selection in this category to nuclei with Q β c ≲ 200 Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}}\lesssim 200 keV and ensuring that more transitions to low-lying states become possible when the Q Q ‑value increases from Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} to Q β b Q_{\beta_{\text{b}}} . Except for the typical example of 187 Re that has been studied in Ref. [ 26 ] , the corresponding heavy nuclei are then listed in Table 2 . The experimental data of log f ​ t ft values of these transitions are shown in the eighth column of Table 4 , and it is seen from Table 4 that these data are described reasonable by our PSM calculations which are listed in the ninth column of Table 4 . In the last column of Table 4 we show the calculated β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives where experimental log f ​ t ft values are adopted whenever available. For 194 Os, 227 Ac, 228 Ra, 241 Pu, and 249 Bk, the experimental log f ​ t ft values for transitions to the ground states or very low-lying states could be as large as about 6 6 , so that the corresponding β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives are determined by these transitions with experimental log f ​ t ft values. The corresponding β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives are on the order of days, while those of other decay modes in neutral atoms are on the order of years. Therefore, these nuclei are of great interest for future experimental studies of nuclear β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay. More interestingly, 247 Cm and 250 Cm exhibit distinctly different behavior. As transuranium nuclei, their decay in neutral atoms is dominated by α \alpha decay and spontaneous fission because the corresponding Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} is as small as about 40 40 keV as seen from Table 2 . However, under highly ionization (i.e., to be hydrogen-like or even bare nuclei), the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay channel opens and rapidly becomes the dominant decay mode. Since the log f ​ t ft values of transitions to the low-lying states are predicted to be as large as about 6 6 and 5 5 for 247 Cm and 250 Cm respectively, their β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives are then predicted to be on the order of days, whereas the corresponding half-lives in neutral atoms are on the order of 10 7 10^{7} and 10 4 10^{4} years respectively. This indicates a dramatic reduction in half-lives for 247 Cm and 250 Cm. It is noted that the half-life of 247 Cm is shortened by up to nine orders of magnitude, while that of 250 Cm is reduced by almost six orders of magnitude. This striking contrast reveals the profound influence of the ionization state on the decay properties of heavy nuclei: isotopes that are conventionally considered as typical α \alpha emitters may, in astrophysical and stellar environments, actually undergo fast β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay. Given the dramatic half-life contraction predicted for these two isotopes, i.e., spanning six to nine orders of magnitude, both 247 Cm and 250 Cm emerge as exceptionally promising candidates for future experimental investigations of β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay.

sections.heading: IV summary
sections.text: In summary, β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay represents an essential decay channel for nuclei immersed in stellar plasmas or heavy-ion storage ring. In this work, we perform a comprehensive survey across the nuclear landscape to identify candidate nuclides that can undergo β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay under highly ionized conditions. Interesting candidates are considered according to two distinct categories: (i) nuclides with negative Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} values in neutral atoms, for which the β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay channel becomes energetically allowed only upon highly ionization; and (ii) nuclides are already unstable with positive Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} values in neutral atoms, while additional transitions are possible since the effective Q Q value is enlarged from Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} to Q β b Q_{\beta_{\text{b}}} . For each category, eight representative nuclides are selected for detailed investigation. Their log ⁡ f ​ t \log ft values are calculated microscopically for the first time, by the PSM where both the allowed GT and first-forbidden transitions are treated on an equal footing. These transition strengths are then combined with phase space factors obtained from the Takahashi-Yokoi model to yield the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives. Our calculations predict that for highly ionized Am 95 + 243 {}^{243}\mathrm{Am}^{95+} , Os 76 + 194 {}^{194}\mathrm{Os}^{76+} , Ac 89 + 227 {}^{227}\mathrm{Ac}^{89+} , Ra 88 + 228 {}^{228}\mathrm{Ra}^{88+} , Pu 94 + 241 {}^{241}\mathrm{Pu}^{94+} , Cm 96 + 247 {}^{247}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} and Cm 96 + 250 {}^{250}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} , the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives are significantly shorter than the corresponding half-lives of other decay modes in neutral atoms. These candidates are therefore recommended for future studies of storage-ring experiments for nuclear β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay. Specifically, among all the candidates studied, particular attention is drawn to 243 Am, 247 Cm, and 250 Cm. For highly ionized 243 Am, the predicted β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay half-life is about 55 days, in striking contrast to its neutral-atom α \alpha -decay half-life of 7345 years — a reduction of nearly five orders of magnitude. For 247 Cm, the half-life plunges from about 10 7 10^{7} years in the neutral state (dominated by α \alpha decay) to merely 0.026 years (9.52 days) under highly ionized conditions, corresponding to a compression of nine orders of magnitude. For 250 Cm, the half-life decreases from about 8300 years to 0.011 years (3.86 days), a reduction of almost six orders of magnitude. These extreme cases vividly demonstrate how the ionization state can fundamentally alter the decay dynamics of heavy nuclei, transforming nuclides conventionally classified as typical α \alpha emitters into rapid β − \beta^{-} decayers in astrophysical environments. The present work provides the first systematic theoretical investigation of β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay half-lives for a diverse set of candidate nuclei within a unified microscopic framework. The predictions provide valuable guidance for future experimental efforts, particularly those at storage-ring facilities, and establish a foundation for more realistic astrophysical simulations in which highly ionized species prevail. Future extensions of this work will incorporate the Saha equation to determine the equilibrium populations of various ionization states under stellar conditions. Acknowledgements. In this work we present a systematic theoretical calculations for the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives of interesting candidates for the first time, where both allowed Gamow-Teller transitions and first-forbidden transitions are taken into account by the microscopic projected shell model, and the lepton phase space is calculated by the Takahashi-Yokoi model. We analyzed the structure informations for hundreds of nuclei near the β \beta -stability line, and select 16 interesting candidates belonging to two categories, i.e., nuclei with negative Q Q values and positive Q Q values in neutral atoms respectively. Among these candidates, we recommend Am 95 + 243 {}^{243}\mathrm{Am}^{95+} , Os 76 + 194 {}^{194}\mathrm{Os}^{76+} , Ac 89 + 227 {}^{227}\mathrm{Ac}^{89+} , Ra 88 + 228 {}^{228}\mathrm{Ra}^{88+} , Pu 94 + 241 {}^{241}\mathrm{Pu}^{94+} , Cm 96 + 247 {}^{247}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} and Cm 96 + 250 {}^{250}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} as promising ones for future studies of storage-ring experiments because their β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives are predicted to be much shorter than the half-lives in neutral atoms. These findings provide essential nuclear inputs for astrophysical models and identify specific candidates where experimental verification would be most valuable. I Introduction Nuclear bound-state β − \beta^{-} decay is one of the novel weak-interaction processes. Different from the continuum β − \beta^{-} decay ( β c \beta_{\text{c}} decay, as shown in Eq. ( 1 a)) where the electron and antineutrino are emitted into the continuum states, in the bound-state β − \beta^{-} decay ( β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay, see Eq. ( 1 b)) provided that atoms get highly ionized to be hydrogen-like or even bare nuclei, the electron is not emitted to the continuum but occupying directly the bound states of electron orbitals of daughter atoms [ 1 ] . The nuclear β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay is important for understanding the nature of neutrinos and the slow ( s s -) neutron-capture processes [ 2 ] . The concept of the β b \beta_{b} decay was first proposed by Daudel et al. in 1947 [ 3 ] . A practical theoretical framework for calculating the β b \beta_{b} -decay half-life of highly ionized atoms was developed by Takahashi and Yokoi in the 1980s [ 4 ] . Over the past decades, experiments at heavy-ion storage rings were conducted and β b \beta_{\text{b}} decays have been observed sequentially in 163 Dy 66+ [ 5 ] , 187 Re 75+ [ 6 ] , 207 Tl 81+ [ 7 ] and 205 Tl 81+ [ 8 , 9 ] . More important candidates of the nuclear β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay are expected to be detected and studied, for which theoretical calculations and analysis should be meaningful. Theoretically, calculations of the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives are basically based on the Takahashi-Yokoi model [ 4 ] where nuclear transition strengths, including both allowed and forbidden transitions, are indispensable key inputs. However, in most of the relevant calculations, unknown nuclear transition strengths are not from sophisticated nuclear many-body calculations, but estimated empirically either from the inverse electron-capture (EC) data, or from the systematics of transitions of neighboring nuclei with available data (from ground states or isomers) [ 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 ] . The former is limited to transitions from ground states of EC parent nuclei, while the latter prescription has been challenged by modern charge-exchange reactions [ 14 ] or shell-model calculations [ 15 ] . This is because most of the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay candidates are heavy nuclei and it is challenging to describe the allowed and forbidden transitions of heavy nuclei. Recently, we developed the traditional projected shell model (PSM) [ 16 , 17 ] to consider extended quasiparticle (qp) configuration space [ 18 , 19 ] , and then to describe allowed Gamow-Teller (GT) transition [ 20 , 21 ] and first-forbidden transition [ 22 ] of nuclear β \beta decay, with the help of the Pfaffian and other algorithms [ 23 , 24 , 25 ] . The extended PSM method is then combined with the Takahashi-Yokoi model to provide a microscopic method to calculate the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives for the first time [ 26 ] . Accordingly, the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives of 163 Dy 66+ and 187 Re 75+ are described successfully and the half-life of 205 Tl 81+ is predicted [ 26 ] . Further systematic calculations and research should be meaningful and beneficial for future experimental studies. In this work, we apply the PSM and Takahashi-Yokoi model to provide a systematic study of the half-lives of nuclear β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay. By analyzing the Q Q values and levels for hundreds of nuclei near the β \beta -stability line on the chart of nuclides, we selected, in addition to the three examples of 163 Dy 66+ , 187 Re 75+ and 205 Tl 81+ examined in the previous study [ 26 ] , sixteen examples for further investigation. These examples are Ir 77 + 193 {}^{193}\mathrm{Ir}^{77+} , Au 79 + 194 {}^{194}\mathrm{Au}^{79+} , Tl 81 + 202 {}^{202}\mathrm{Tl}^{81+} , Po 84 + 213 {}^{213}\mathrm{Po}^{84+} , At 85 + 215 {}^{215}\mathrm{At}^{85+} , Rn 86 + 222 {}^{222}\mathrm{Rn}^{86+} , Am 95 + 243 {}^{243}\mathrm{Am}^{95+} , and Bk 97 + 246 {}^{246}\mathrm{Bk}^{97+} , as well as Os 76 + 194 {}^{194}\mathrm{Os}^{76+} , At 85 + 212 {}^{212}\mathrm{At}^{85+} , Ac 89 + 227 {}^{227}\mathrm{Ac}^{89+} , Ra 88 + 228 {}^{228}\mathrm{Ra}^{88+} , Pu 94 + 241 {}^{241}\mathrm{Pu}^{94+} , Cm 96 + 247 {}^{247}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} , Bk 97 + 249 {}^{249}\mathrm{Bk}^{97+} , and Cm 96 + 250 {}^{250}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} . IV summary In summary, β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay represents an essential decay channel for nuclei immersed in stellar plasmas or heavy-ion storage ring. In this work, we perform a comprehensive survey across the nuclear landscape to identify candidate nuclides that can undergo β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay under highly ionized conditions. Interesting candidates are considered according to two distinct categories: (i) nuclides with negative Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} values in neutral atoms, for which the β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay channel becomes energetically allowed only upon highly ionization; and (ii) nuclides are already unstable with positive Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} values in neutral atoms, while additional transitions are possible since the effective Q Q value is enlarged from Q β c Q_{\beta_{\text{c}}} to Q β b Q_{\beta_{\text{b}}} . For each category, eight representative nuclides are selected for detailed investigation. Their log ⁡ f ​ t \log ft values are calculated microscopically for the first time, by the PSM where both the allowed GT and first-forbidden transitions are treated on an equal footing. These transition strengths are then combined with phase space factors obtained from the Takahashi-Yokoi model to yield the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives. Our calculations predict that for highly ionized Am 95 + 243 {}^{243}\mathrm{Am}^{95+} , Os 76 + 194 {}^{194}\mathrm{Os}^{76+} , Ac 89 + 227 {}^{227}\mathrm{Ac}^{89+} , Ra 88 + 228 {}^{228}\mathrm{Ra}^{88+} , Pu 94 + 241 {}^{241}\mathrm{Pu}^{94+} , Cm 96 + 247 {}^{247}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} and Cm 96 + 250 {}^{250}\mathrm{Cm}^{96+} , the β b \beta_{\text{b}} -decay half-lives are significantly shorter than the corresponding half-lives of other decay modes in neutral atoms. These candidates are therefore recommended for future studies of storage-ring experiments for nuclear β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay. Specifically, among all the candidates studied, particular attention is drawn to 243 Am, 247 Cm, and 250 Cm. For highly ionized 243 Am, the predicted β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay half-life is about 55 days, in striking contrast to its neutral-atom α \alpha -decay half-life of 7345 years — a reduction of nearly five orders of magnitude. For 247 Cm, the half-life plunges from about 10 7 10^{7} years in the neutral state (dominated by α \alpha decay) to merely 0.026 years (9.52 days) under highly ionized conditions, corresponding to a compression of nine orders of magnitude. For 250 Cm, the half-life decreases from about 8300 years to 0.011 years (3.86 days), a reduction of almost six orders of magnitude. These extreme cases vividly demonstrate how the ionization state can fundamentally alter the decay dynamics of heavy nuclei, transforming nuclides conventionally classified as typical α \alpha emitters into rapid β − \beta^{-} decayers in astrophysical environments. The present work provides the first systematic theoretical investigation of β b \beta_{\text{b}} decay half-lives for a diverse set of candidate nuclei within a unified microscopic framework. The predictions provide valuable guidance for future experimental efforts, particularly those at storage-ring facilities, and establish a foundation for more realistic astrophysical simulations in which highly ionized species prevail.
